label: one or two steps after an early m in the original sequence
explanation: Fires during the original-input phase at the step right after the letter m is input (prev_tok == m: 44% firing rate, 18x lift, 78% of activation mass), with a weaker tail one step later (prev2_tok == m, 24% of mass). Strongest when m is input twice in a row early in the sequence (e.g. g m m -> next step near max). Activation is highest when the m comes early (t = 2-4) and fades by t >= 6, so an m late in the sequence produces little or no activation. Essentially never fires in the copy phase, rarely on the delimiter (1.6% of mass), and never at t = 0. Leftover small activations (lowest quartile) scatter across steps 3-5 with no m nearby.

issues: The test scores reproduce: P 0.924, R 0.760, F1 0.834, mass recall 0.949. Dev scores are almost the same.

The factual claims check out. The copy phase has 0 activations. t=0 has 0 activations. The delimiter holds 1.6% of the mass. prev_tok==m has 44% rate, 18x lift and 78% of the mass. prev2_tok==m holds 23-24% of the mass. Activation dies out from t=6 on (1.3% of mass at t=6, about 0 from t=7).
The 18x lift and 44% rate for prev_tok==m are counted over all phases. Restricted to phase 0, prev_tok==m has precision 0.85.

False positives are moderately systematic but small (precision is still 0.92). They are mainly prev2_tok==m steps where the m is at t=0, or where the m comes at t=4-5 and the next steps stay silent. Dropping prev2 at t=2 raises precision to 0.94, but test F1 falls to 0.79, so the original predicate is the better trade-off.

Missed activations hold 5% of the mass and are mostly tiny. A few sit next to an m, for example on <DEL> right after a final m or at t=6 after an m. That slightly contradicts the claim that the leftovers have 'no m nearby', but it is minor.
The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
